name: Video ad, from idea to signed-off final cut
goal: A finished, on-brand video ad in 9:16 and 4:5, made from a script you approved, with real product shots, captions and an end card, ready for the launch team.
starts_from: A growth plan task, a creative refresh brief from the results review, or you asking for a new video ad.
metrics: Main number: the one you set in context/goals.json (for most stores, return on ad spend over 7 days).
Video numbers: hook rate (3-second views divided by impressions), hold rate (ThruPlays divided by 3-second views), and click-through rate.
Cost: money spent on generation for this video, against the estimate you approved.

stages.name: Gather what we know
stages.say: Collects every fact the video needs before anyone writes a word: who it is for, what problem it solves for them, the product facts and claims we can prove, the offer, what past videos taught us, and which connectors and files we can reach. Anything missing is listed as a question for you. It also writes channels.json: the launch processes this creative will go to (for example ["meta-launch", "tiktok-ads-launch"]), from the placements in the task or the growth plan.
needs: context/org-context/ (customers, voice, design, claims, do's and don'ts)
the task that started this job
stages.done_when: intake.md names the buyer, the gap we are solving, the one message, the proof we hold, the offer, the placement, and the open questions you answered.

stages.name: Angle and script
stages.say: Writes three hook options and one full script: beats with timings, voice-over, on-screen text, the product moment, proof, and the call to action. It follows direct-response rules: the first two seconds earn the next five, one idea per ad, and every claim traces to the proof in intake.md.
stages.signoff: You read the three hooks, the script and the small pre-production budget. Reply yes with the code to lock them. To change anything, say what; the code stops working as soon as a file changes.
stages.done_when: script.md has three hooks, timed beats that add up to the planned length, and every claim marked with its proof.
stages.spends: Sets the pre-production budget: storyboard frames and reference sheets, usually a few dollars of images.

stages.name: Shot list and storyboard prompts
stages.say: Turns the locked script into a shot list: one row per shot with duration, framing, camera move, action, on-screen text and sound. Then writes one image prompt per shot for quick storyboard frames.
stages.done_when: Every script beat maps to at least one shot, durations add up to the script length, and each shot has a prompt.

stages.name: Rough storyboard frames
stages.say: Makes a quick still frame for each shot and lays them out on one contact sheet, so you can see the flow of the ad before any video money is spent.
stages.signoff: You look at the contact sheet. Reply yes with the code if the flow works, or say which shots to change.
stages.done_when: There is one frame per shot on the contact sheet, in script order, each labelled with its shot number.

stages.name: Character and product reference sheets
stages.say: Fixes how every person in the ad looks (face, age, clothes, setting) on a character sheet, and builds a product reference sheet from your real product photos, so every scene shows the same people and the true product, label and colours.
stages.signoff: You check the people match your buyers and the product looks exactly like yours. Reply yes with the code.
stages.done_when: Each person has front and side views and a written description, and the product sheet uses your real photos, not a redrawn product.

stages.name: Final storyboard
stages.say: Redraws the storyboard frames using the character and product sheets, so each frame now shows the right people and the real product. These frames become the first frame or reference image for each video scene.
stages.done_when: Every frame matches its character and product sheet, and the shot order is unchanged from the signed-off rough storyboard.

stages.name: Scenes, prompts and model choice
stages.spends: Raises the budget to cover video generation. cost-estimate.json is updated to the new total, and nothing is generated until you approve it.
stages.say: Splits the ad into scenes. For each scene it writes the video prompt, the reference frame, the length, the camera move and the sound, and picks the video model that suits it (for example one model for people talking, another for product close-ups). It estimates the cost, with at most two retries per scene, and lists it for you.
stages.signoff: You see each scene, the model chosen and the total cost. Reply yes with the code to approve that budget. Generation stops if it would go over.
stages.done_when: scenes.json covers every shot, and cost-estimate.json gives a total with the price source and date for each model.

stages.name: Generate the scenes
stages.say: Generates each scene with its chosen model and reference frame. Each clip is checked against its scene: right people, real product, readable label, no warped hands or text. A clip that fails gets at most two retries, inside the approved budget, then the scene goes back to you.
stages.done_when: Every scene has one approved clip listed in clips/clips.md with its model and retries, and spend.json records what each generation cost.

stages.name: Edit and merge
stages.say: Puts the clips in order, trims to the script timings, adds the voice-over and licensed music, and makes the cut feel fast in the first three seconds. Exports a rough cut for checking.
stages.done_when: The rough cut matches the script beats within half a second each, and the music licence is written in edit-notes.md.

stages.name: Captions, graphics and end card
stages.say: Adds captions word for word from the script, on-screen text, the real logo laid on by the editing tool (never redrawn by a model), the offer and the end card. Makes a 9:16 version for Reels and Stories and a 4:5 version for feeds, with text inside the safe zones.
stages.done_when: Both versions exist, captions match the script, the logo passes the contrast check, and no text sits in the top or bottom safe zones.

stages.name: Final review and sign-off
stages.say: A fresh reviewer who did not make the ad watches it against the intake and script: on brand, the hook lands in the first two seconds, claims are proven, the product is true to life. The compliance reviewer checks ad policy, music rights and whether the ad must be marked as made with AI. It also writes tags.json (concept, angle, hook type, format, length in seconds, persona, model used) so results can be compared by what was made. Before your sign-off it confirms channels.json, so your yes covers where the creative will run. Each channel gets its own launch job in the same folder.
stages.signoff: You watch both versions. Reply yes with the code to sign off. The video then goes to the launch team with its script and review.
stages.done_when: review.md records PASS from both reviewers, the AI disclosure answer, and the licence notes, and your sign-off covers every file in final/ byte for byte.

intake-complete.passes_when: every heading in intake.md is filled from a named source, and missing facts are listed as answered questions, not guesses

script-review.passes_when: the hook earns attention in two seconds, there is one idea, the voice matches the Org context, and every claim maps to proof

copy-lint.passes_when: the copy checker exits 0 (no banned words, no made-up stats, reading level in range)

storyboard-review.passes_when: every beat has a shot, timings add up, and each prompt describes the frame without inventing product details

storyboard-visual.passes_when: the frames read in order as a story with the product moment clear, and nothing contradicts the design rules

consistency-review.passes_when: people look the same in every frame and the product matches the real photos, label text included

scene-plan-review.passes_when: every scene can be cut together at the planned lengths, and each model choice has a reason

clip-review.passes_when: each clip matches its scene, the product and label are true, and there are no warped hands, faces or text

spend-within-budget.passes_when: money spent on generation (spend.json) is at or under the approved estimate (cost-estimate.json)

cut-review.passes_when: the cut follows the script beats, the first three seconds move fast, and the sound is clean

graphics-review.passes_when: captions match the script word for word, fonts and colours follow the design rules, and text stays in the safe zones

logo-contrast.passes_when: the logo contrast ratio is at least 3 to 1

creative-review.passes_when: a reviewer who did not make the ad finds it on brand, on message and true to the product

compliance-review.passes_when: no policy problems, music is licensed, claims are proven, and the AI disclosure answer is recorded
